title: Design a URL Shortener
interviewPrompt: For today's Software Engineer interview, design a URL shortener.

beats.interviewer: For today's Software Engineer interview, design a URL shortener.
beats.interviewee: Complete naive system first: take a long URL, hash it, store code-to-URL in a key-value store, redirect on lookup. Three boxes, end to end.
beats.show: Naive complete: Client → API → KV. Hash, store, redirect.

beats.interviewer: Say it gets popular. What breaks first?
beats.interviewee: Same full path under pressure. Hash is too long, truncating collides, and the hot write becomes the ceiling.
beats.show: Same complete path. Collisions + write bottleneck.

beats.interviewer: Let's go deeper on the code generation. Fix it.
beats.interviewee: Rework the middle: hand out a unique 64-bit ID from a counter, base62-encode it. Still Client → API → KV, now with a dedicated ID gen.
beats.show: Rework: Counter → base62. Full path still shortens and resolves.

beats.interviewer: Is a central counter the only option?
beats.interviewee: No. Salt or Hashids for unguessable codes, or pre-allocate ID ranges per server. Same complete system, different ID strategy.
beats.show: Same complete system. ID strategy tradeoffs only.

beats.interviewee: Reads beat writes about 100 to 1. Keep the mapping in DynamoDB, add Redis read-through for hot links. Full shorten + resolve path still works.
beats.show: Add Redis hot-link cache. Complete path: API → cache → KV.
